# True or false

163 statements about the playbook, in 16 areas. Some are myths that sound right; others are facts that sound wrong. Each answer explains why in a few sentences and links to the page that teaches the practice.

Play on GitHub by opening an area below, or in a terminal from the repository root:

```bash
python3 exercises/quiz.py                       # 10 random statements
python3 exercises/quiz.py --area security ai    # only these areas
python3 exercises/quiz.py --level foundation    # only one level
python3 exercises/quiz.py --count 0 --seed 7    # every statement, repeatable order
python3 exercises/quiz.py --save results.jsonl  # keep a record of each session
python3 exercises/quiz.py --retry-missed results.jsonl  # replay last session's misses
```

The terminal quiz keeps a running score, shows your result by area and suggests three pages to read next.

| Area | Statements | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| [Strategy](strategy.md) | 10 | Most engineering waste starts here: goals with no diagnosis, tools chosen before problems, and work that never stops. See how well you can tell a real strategy from a wish list. |
| [Operating model](operating-model.md) | 10 | Who decides, who is consulted and how teams are shaped set the speed of everything else. These statements test the beliefs that slow organisations down. |
| [Ways of working](ways-of-working.md) | 10 | Story points, velocity, sprints and estimates: some of the most repeated beliefs in software are not in the Scrum Guide at all. Find out which ones. |
| [Delivery](delivery.md) | 10 | Branches, pipelines, reviews, migrations and releases. Small, frequent, reversible changes are the theme; check whether your habits agree. |
| [Quality](quality.md) | 10 | Quality is built in while the code is written, not inspected at the end. These statements check what you believe about testers, TDD and test suites. |
| [Reliability](reliability.md) | 11 | SLOs, on-call, incidents, rollbacks and backups. Several of these statements sound responsible and make outages longer. |
| [Security](security.md) | 11 | Vulnerabilities, secrets, dependencies, zero trust and the quantum timeline. Separate the controls that work from the ones that only feel safe. |
| [Data](data.md) | 10 | Ownership, classification, quality and privacy. Most data problems are ownership problems; see which common habits make them worse. |
| [AI](ai.md) | 10 | Prompt injection, evaluations, agents and the EU AI Act. Building with AI changes less than people think, and the parts it does change matter a lot. |
| [Architecture](architecture.md) | 11 | Microservices, rewrites, decision records, APIs and debt. Test your instincts on the decisions that are expensive to reverse. |
| [Platform](platform.md) | 10 | Kubernetes, golden paths, developer platforms, cloud cost and carbon. The simplest option that meets the need wins more often than people expect. |
| [People](people.md) | 10 | Code assistants, hiring, onboarding, careers and sustainable pace. These statements test beliefs about how engineers join, grow and stay. |
| [Measurement](measurement.md) | 10 | DORA metrics, SPACE and the maturity model. Metrics help teams choose what to improve, and hurt them the moment they become targets for people. |
| [Compliance](compliance.md) | 10 | Auditors, regulators and public-sector rules. Good engineering evidence answers most of their questions without extra meetings. |
| [Leaders](leaders.md) | 10 | For CTOs, CIOs, architects and executives: decisions, crises, boards and portfolios. Test the beliefs that shape how technology is led. |
| [Business owners](business-owners.md) | 10 | For owners and managers of clinics, schools, shops and other businesses that use software but do not build it. No technical knowledge needed. |

To add or change a statement, edit [questions.toml](questions.toml), then run `python3 exercises/quiz.py --export` and `python3 exercises/quiz.py --check`.
